svg.title: Arbitr architecture, animated (light theme)
svg.desc: AI agents (Claude, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, and MCP clients such as Claude Code and Cursor) call tools through an integration layer: a @guard decorator, an Anthropic tool-use helper, an OpenAI Agents SDK adapter, a LangGraph tool node, an MCP proxy, or an HTTP API. Every call enters the Arbitr core and passes five stages in order: 1, canonicalize and compute intent (RFC 8785 JSON, intent hash, idempotency key); 2, write-ahead ledger (recorded before anything runs, explicit state machine); 3, deterministic gate (policy rules, resource tags, budgets, run taint, no LLM in the decision) with outcomes allow, deny, or require approval; 4, approvals (bound to the exact call, HMAC token, expiry); 5, executor (runs once in effect using leases, idempotency keys, crash recovery, and probes), which acts on the real world: databases, cloud, payments, email, GitHub, and shell. Supporting modules: a redactor so secrets are never stored, a compensator for undo, and a tamper-evident audit chain. The core persists to SQLite in WAL mode or Postgres, which feed a CLI, a local dashboard, a shadow report, and OpenTelemetry spans. The animation loops through three example calls: opening a GitHub pull request is allowed and runs; a $500 refund requires approval, is approved, then runs; an rm -rf on the shell is denied and never runs. Each call is recorded in the ledger and the audit chain.
svg.text: every call flows through the ledger first
how a tool call reaches Arbitr

g.text: Example call: open a pull request on GitHub: allowed
